page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose instance featuring 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance. The processor features 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, along with support for AES, SHA_NI cryptographic acceleration, and AVX instruction sets.

Benchmark results indicate solid single-threaded performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2647.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1484.0. Multi-core capacity is limited by the single-vCPU ceiling, and uncached memory read bandwidth measures 21.24 GB/sec. Small LLM text generation with a 135M parameter model executes at 85.18 tokens per second, while static web serving throughput measures 1.73 GB/sec.

The instance includes no local storage or attached GPUs, relying entirely on attached network storage. The dedicated thread allocation prevents CPU credit exhaustion associated with burstable classes, delivering steady performance for basic web services, microservices, micro-databases, and lightweight background automation tasks.
